_purpose: Pre-holdout architecture freeze manifest, V3 -- supersedes V2 (LNES59_PRE_HOLDOUT_CODE_MANIFEST_V2.json) for holdout-gating purposes. V1 and V2 both preserved unmodified, not deleted, for chronology. This freeze exists specifically because Phase 5 development red-teaming found a real architecture defect -- permitted under the Trustee directive's Section 6 process precisely because holdout has not been evaluated yet.

lineage.reason: initial pre-holdout freeze after closing the last two disclosed extraction limitations (scope, historical values)
resolved B3-002/B2-006 predicate semantics + third scope case + CandidateClaim architecture documentation -- no code changes, dataset/docs only

Phase 5 development red-teaming found a genuine extraction-layer defect (taxonomy #19) in a NEW case, not any of the original 27 -- the first defect this project has found in NEW development data rather than architecture-design work

why_a_v3_freeze_was_needed: Taxonomy #19: _UNAVAILABLE_MARKERS' bare word 'maintenance' collided with ordinary business vocabulary ('equipment maintenance contract') in LNES59-B4-002's original PO document, misclassifying it INCOMPLETE and collapsing an entire 3-hop supersession chain. A genuine, general extraction defect -- not specific to one case, would affect any future document using 'maintenance' in its ordinary business sense. Narrowed the marker to the specific multi-word phrasing the real system-status documents use ('scheduled maintenance', 'maintenance window'), verified against both the real system-status document (still matches) and the colliding PO document (no longer matches).

explicitly_not_frozen.cases.json / cases_batch2-4.json / docum: dataset content, not architecture -- documents_batch4.json/cases_batch4.json are Phase 5 tranche 1 (4 new DEVELOPMENT cases), MORE tranches follow under these same frozen rules
explicitly_not_frozen.run_case.py, arm_x2.py, run_x2_arm.py, m: harness/runner code -- loader functions were updated this pass to include batch4 files, not a frozen-architecture change
explicitly_not_frozen.test_*.py: test files grow with the dataset -- test_no_match_stress.py and test_open_world_claim_types.py are new this pass, characterizing new development cases, not changing frozen behavior

gate._version_note: UNCHANGED from V2/V1 -- same file, same hash. Taxonomy #19 was an extraction-layer defect, not a gate defect.

extraction._version_note: 1.2 = V2 freeze. 1.3 = this freeze -- taxonomy #19 fix (_UNAVAILABLE_MARKERS narrowed from bare 'maintenance' to 'scheduled maintenance'/'maintenance window'). First extraction change since V1.

regression_suite_state_at_freeze._total: 169/169, all green at the frozen commit

dataset_state_at_freeze._note: All 31 cases (27 original + 4 new) are DEVELOPMENT-TAINTED -- every one has now either informed architecture decisions or characterized the frozen architecture against real red-team fixtures. None are holdout-eligible. Phase 5 continues with further tranches.

known_remaining_limitations_at_freeze: Sparse (2-word) NO_MATCH value tokens whose negation marker does NOT survive the word-length filter (e.g. NO_APPROVAL_ON_RECORD, where 'NO' is dropped for being 2 letters) remain vulnerable to a vague hedge false-matching -- confirmed narrower than first thought via test_no_match_stress.py: tokens like NOT_IN_REGISTRY (where 'NOT' survives) are NOT vulnerable to the same class of hedge. Not fixed -- Phase 5 case authoring should prefer NOT_X over NO_X phrasing for new NO_MATCH predicates where practical.
CandidateClaim architecture remains design-only, unchanged since V2.
PREDICATE_ALIAS category remains unused in the corpus, unchanged since V2.
No B0-B4 baseline or full X0-X1 sweep has been run -- X2 remains the only arm with real empirical data, unchanged since V1/V2.

The directive's Phase 11 4th open-world variant (ACTION_REQUEST against an unrelated authority predicate) was deliberately not folded into test_open_world_claim_types.py -- would need its own compare_against_predicate wiring, not yet built.
